candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Official provider announcement checked September 24; event date bound by the saved original capture.

claims.claim: Anthropic publishes $4 input and $20 output prices per million API tokens.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: input costs $4 and output $20 per million tokens.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Input and output tokens are $4 and $20 per million, 20% less than Opus 5. Cache reads (which make up the majority of agentic and coding work costs) are $0.20 per million tokens, 60% less than Opus 5.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Developer usage pricing for customers paying Anthropic directly, not a monthly subscription or third-party app price.

claims.claim: Anthropic says five-hour limits increased for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise, and subscription users receive a saveable reset.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: In addition to the price drop, we’re increasing five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. We’re also providing subscription users a rate limit reset, which you can now save and use whenever you choose.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Provider plan statement; announcement does not quantify the limits or establish identical selector access.

claims.claim: Anthropic positions Opus 5.5 for moving a software project to a new system or reviewing its code; this does not make it the default for simple work.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is best suited to moving a software project to a new system or reviewing its code.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Opus 5.5 is particularly good at long and sprawling jobs like codebase-wide migrations and audits.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: The task positioning is Anthropic’s; the simple-task alternative is editorial interpretation, not a benchmark result.

claims.claim: The announcement does not provide a plan-by-plan ordinary-chat model-selector map.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The announcement does not quantify those limits or map ordinary Claude-chat model-selector access plan by plan.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with `claude-opus-5-5`.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Bounded source-gap statement; current account UI and plan documentation remain necessary for account-specific access.
